newsitem.title: USA: U.S. soft red winter wheat reported in good shape.
newsitem.headline: U.S. soft red winter wheat reported in good shape.

text.p: Weekly state crop reports issued on Monday said the U.S. soft red winter wheat crop in major states was generally in good shape and ahead of last year's growth pace in the week ended Sunday.
A summary of agricultural statistics service reports:

OHIO - Wheat was rated 47 percent good to excellent versus 46 percent a week earlier, with 36 percent rated fair. Wheat rated poor or very poor was 15 percent, versus 22 last week. "Wheat diseases are minimal throughout the state at this time," said Pat Lipps of Ohio State University extension service, who reported some minor losses from frost heaving.

INDIANA - Wheat was rated 63 percent good to excellent versus 57 percent a week earlier, with 28 percent rated fair. Nine percent of the crop was rated poor or very poor, unchanged and compared to 48 percent in that range in 1996. Last year at this time, 20 percent of the crop was rated good to excellent. About 52 percent of wheat was jointed, ahead of 27 last week, 23 last year and the five-year average of 38 percent. Soil moisture levels fell slightly but were still 90 percent adequate/surplus for topsoil and 96 pct for subsoil.
ILLINOIS - Wheat was rated 72 percent good to excellent, 22 percent fair and six percent poor to very poor.

"Growth of wheat, pasture and hay crops has been slow due to cool temperatures and frequent overnight frosts," the Illinois agricultural statistics service said in its update. Statewide, topsoil moisture was rated 18 percent surplus and 74 adequate.

MISSOURI - Wheat was rated 63 percent good to excellent, 26 percent fair, and 11 percent poor to very poor, slightly improved from a week earlier. Six percent of the crop was headed compared with none at the same time last year and four percent on a five-year average. Most of the headed wheat was confined to the bootheel region. Most favorable ratings were in the north central, west central, east central and southwestern districts. Topsoil moisture was rated 41 percent surplus and 56 percent adequate.
